headline: A Fortune commentary argues that Sam Altman has history backwards in hoping for an AI "Renaissance", and that regulating AI would shield big companies.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a prominent counter-argument on AI regulation, but it is one writer's opinion answering a 23 Sep speech.
importance_line: It feeds the debate over who should write AI rules, which affects everyone who uses AI, but it is opinion and its historical claims are the author's, not independently checked.
summary: Fortune publishes a commentary answering a 23 Sep speech to the United Nations by OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, who said AI could be "a new Renaissance of creativity and discovery" or "a new Industrial Revolution of upheaval and disarray" and called for international standards. The author argues the Industrial Revolution, not the Renaissance, delivered lasting gains and that AI rules of the kind Altman hinted at would cement the power of existing companies, including his own; this is opinion, not reported fact.
notes: Reply story: names Altman's 23 Sep UN speech (not carried by us). Opinion piece.
